classification.difficultyReason: Supplied construction still requires selecting the isosceles triangle, deriving similarity ratios and algebraic cancellation, then generalising twice including product cancellation; integrated strategic proof supports Mastery.

children.label: a
children.prompt: In $\triangle ABC$, AD bisects $\angle BAC$. Prove that $\dfrac{BD}{DC}=\dfrac{BA}{AC}$. Hint: Construct CE parallel to DA to meet BA extended at E.

spec.description: Actual triangleABC/D onBC, AD exact internal anglebisector with twoalpha labels; no numerical angles/lengths or extra equal-side/rightangle givens.
spec.mathematics: Actual triangleABC/D onBC, AD exact internal anglebisector with twoalpha labels; no numerical angles/lengths or extra equal-side/rightangle givens.

answer.worked: Construct CE as hinted. With $AD\parallel CE$ and B,A,E collinear, $\triangle BAD\sim\triangle BEC$ by AAA. Also $\angle AEC=\angle BAD$ and $\angle ACE=\angle DAC$; these are equal because AD bisects angle A. Thus triangle AEC is isosceles and AE=AC. Corresponding sides give $$\frac{BD}{BD+DC}=\frac{BA}{BA+AE}=\frac{BA}{BA+AC}.$$ Cross-multiplying gives $BD(BA+AC)=BA(BD+DC)$. Subtracting $BD\cdot BA$ from both sides leaves $BD\cdot AC=BA\cdot DC$, so $\frac{BD}{DC}=\frac{BA}{AC}$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: The bisectors of angle A and angle C of a quadrilateral ABCD meet at a point E on the diagonal BD. Prove that $\dfrac{AD}{AB}=\dfrac{CD}{CB}$.

answer.worked: Apply part a in triangle ABD, where AE bisects angle A: $\frac{BE}{ED}=\frac{AB}{AD}$. Apply part a in triangle CBD, where CE bisects angle C: $\frac{BE}{ED}=\frac{CB}{CD}$. Therefore $\frac{AB}{AD}=\frac{CB}{CD}$. Taking reciprocals gives $\frac{AD}{AB}=\frac{CD}{CB}$.

children.label: c
children.prompt: The bisectors of the angles A, B and C of $\triangle ABC$ meet the opposite sides at D, E and F. Prove that $\dfrac{BD}{DC}\times\dfrac{CE}{EA}\times\dfrac{AF}{FB}=1$.

answer.worked: Apply part a at each vertex: $$\frac{BD}{DC}=\frac{BA}{AC},\qquad\frac{CE}{EA}=\frac{BC}{BA},\qquad\frac{AF}{FB}=\frac{AC}{BC}.$$ Multiplying and cancelling the positive side lengths gives $$\frac{BD}{DC}\times\frac{CE}{EA}\times\frac{AF}{FB}=\frac{BA}{AC}\times\frac{BC}{BA}\times\frac{AC}{BC}=1.$$
